promotion_note: PROMOTED 2026-08-04 (miso-126). MISO keeper -> 2026-08-04-miso-126-steampart-b (bundle results/calibration/miso126_steampart_B). THE SINGLE DELTA AGAINST THE PREDECESSOR 2026-08-04-miso-124-dualfuel-rearm IS ONE ScenarioConfig KEY: cc_steam_part_capacity false -> true, applied via replay_keeper --set and visible in run_config.json (rule 26 [R-REGISTRY]); a programmatic diff of the two scenario blocks returns exactly one differing key, and it is scored against a SAME-HEAD ZERO-DELTA CONTROL (2026-08-04-miso-126-steampart-control), never against the committed predecessor bundle. WHAT IT FIXES: 250 MW of PUBLISHED, OPERABLE MISO capacity that never reached the LP at all. EIA-860's Energy Source 1 on a CA (combined-cycle steam part) row names the block's SUPPLEMENTARY / DUCT fuel, not its primary energy input, which arrives as its own combustion turbines' exhaust -- so 55088 Dearborn ST1 (prime mover CA, Unit Code SINT shared with the two NG CT turbines that drive it, Energy Source 1 BFG) reported an exotic fuel code, fleet.eia860._map_fuel_type returned None, and the row was skipped. The plant sat in the fleet at 515.0 MW against an EIA-860 total of 765.0 MW. THE RATE WAS ALREADY RIGHT AND IS NOT CHANGED: eGRID's PLNGENAN of 5,259,825 net MWh implies an IMPOSSIBLE 116.6 % capacity factor on 515.0 MW and 78.5 % on the repaired 765.0 MW, so the incumbent measured-CHP rate's denominator already counted the missing machine -- it was a BLOCK rate applied to two thirds of the block. The paired re-derive of chp_power_only_heat_rates_MISO.csv (rule 23 [R-FROZEN-DERIVE], cited to the fleet/denominator change, never to a residual) moves exactly ONE cell, class_capacity_mw at (55088, CC_CHP) 350.0 -> 600.0; every applied rate and flag is byte-identical, and a flag-off control re-derive reproduces the committed artifact byte-for-byte. IDENTIFICATION IS THE PRE-REGISTRATION, NOT THE RESULT (results/calibration/PREREG-miso126-cc-steam-part-capacity-2026-08-04.md, pushed before any adjudicating statistic). Five numbered properties, each with its own falsifier, all evaluated BEFORE any solve: P1 absence PASS; P2 one-meter-one-rate PASS at 55088 but FALSIFIED at 50973 Motiva (present-fleet implied CF already 80.1 %, so the denominator evidence is absent -- not contrary, insufficient), which is why the lever is 250.0 MW and NOT the 290.4 MW miso-125 named; P3 design-share coherence PASS, closing miso-125 §4's let-down-turbine doubt BY MEASUREMENT (ST1's implied generation share of its block 0.4173 against its EIA-860 NAMEPLATE design share 0.4307, gap 0.0134 against a pre-declared 0.10 band); P4 artifact stability PASS; P5 ISO scope PASS (MISO +1 generator, ERCOT/CAISO/PJM/NYISO/NEISO fleets BYTE-IDENTICAL). ZERO free parameters: every clause of the predicate is an equality on a published EIA-860 categorical field plus one physical vintage inequality, and the restored generator takes the block's existing heat rate, so the mechanism introduces no new numeric value at all. 1004 Edwardsport matches the predicate and is UNTOUCHED -- its technology string carries 'coal' so it is already in the fleet as COAL 555.0 MW, and the repair only ever RESTORES a row the fuel map drops. A WIRING GAP WAS FOUND AND CLOSED BEFORE THIS RESULT WAS BELIEVED. The first arm-B solve came back EXACTLY inert -- zero class-energy and zero price delta to machine precision -- because the flag was not forwarded at the BACKCAST's own copy of the bin synthesis (scripts/run_calibration.py), the nyiso-89 regression class the code comment at that site explicitly warns about. Fixed, re-solved, and the durable remedy shipped with it: the pre-existing wiring guard pinned only measured_ct_heat_rates, so it is generalised to EVERY boolean ScenarioConfig-backed keyword of load_fleet_from_csv, verified to FAIL against the pre-fix source. MEASURED, AGAINST THE ZERO-DELTA CONTROL: CC_CHP +1,013.7 / +1,149.7 / +1,073.3 GWh in 2023 / 2024 / 2025, displacing CT_PEAKER, CC_REGULAR, COAL_PRB, imports, ST_GAS and COAL_BIT; max zonal |dLMP| 18.578 / 1.328 / 12.267 $/MWh over 7,179 / 7,608 / 8,077 hours; system demand-weighted dLMP -0.0805 / -0.0812 / -0.1005 $/MWh, one-sided downward as adding deep-inframarginal capacity requires (checked, not assumed). Energy conservation holds on the full identity to -0.010 / +0.054 / +0.031 GWh on a ~650 TWh system. NOTHING REGRESSES AND C1 MATERIALLY IMPROVES: determination NOT-YET, all NINE criterion statuses and the ledgered-caveat budget {C3a, C3c} IDENTICAL to the predecessor, C7 COAL_PRB still the sole FAIL, C1 all 16/16 free 12/12, and ZERO legitimacy-diagnostic verdict changes across D-1/D-2/D-4/D-5/D-9/D-10. C1 CC_CHP absolute error collapses -1.55 -> -0.53 TWh (2023) and -1.61 -> -0.46 TWh (2024) -- 68 % and 71 % of that class's entire error, exactly as a missing-capacity repair should, since the EIA-923 benchmark target already counted ST1's generation. Summed C1 |error| over all scored (class, year) rows improves 37.20 -> 35.46 TWh. C3a mean LMP drifts 0.3 pp further negative in each year (-1.1 -> -1.4 %, -6.4 -> -6.6 %, -14.2 -> -14.5 %) with NO status change; that is kept per rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 14 [R-ACCURATE] rather than reverting an accurate input, and it is routed to MISO's already-ledgered C3a root cause (the deterministic-LP scarcity-tail limitation), not treated as a defect of this repair. A/B gates K0-K7 ALL PASS (results/calibration/_miso126_steam_part_ab.json). ONE PRE-REGISTERED STATISTIC WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS CORRECTED RATHER THAN LOOSENED: K6 energy conservation was written on the summed CLASS-energy delta, which fails (+0.39 / +2.06 / -1.31 GWh against a 0.5 GWh band) because the class sidecar excludes storage charge/discharge and unserved energy, both of which this lever legitimately moves. The full identity is reported and carries the verdict; the session's own miso-125 lesson turned on itself -- a magnitude that violates a conservation law is a BOUNDARY defect in the statistic before it is a result. Promoted on structural fidelity (rules 1 / 14), never on a score. NOTHING is claimed for any criterion and C7 COAL_PRB is untouched. Leave-one-year-out (rule 22): the mechanism has zero fitted parameters and nothing year-specific, and its effect is independently present and same-signed in all three years (and C1 improves in both scored years separately), so no single year carries the result. Rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: ISO-gated on plant_taxonomy.CC_STEAM_PART_REPAIR_ISOS = {MISO}; CAISO 54912 Martinez STG1 (20.0 MW) and NEISO 6081 Stony Brook CA1 (96.0 MW) are reported and HANDED OFF UNSTAMPED to their own lanes. Rule 22 [R-HOLDOUT]: 2023-2025 only -- MISO holds no calibration-complete marker, so no out-of-training year was solved, scored or read and the D-5(b) re-key duty does not apply.
note:
THIS KEEPER'S OWN DELTA (miso-126): MISO's fleet now contains a 250 MW combined-cycle STEAM turbine it had been silently dropping. EIA-860 55088 Dearborn ST1 -- prime mover CA, Unit Code SINT shared with the two NG CT turbines whose exhaust drives it, Energy Source 1 BFG -- is half of an ordinary gas-fired combined cycle, but EIA-860's Energy Source 1 on a CA row describes the block's SUPPLEMENTARY/DUCT fuel rather than its primary energy input, so the fuel-type map returned None and the row never reached the LP. The plant ran at 515.0 MW against a published 765.0 MW. The heat rate needed no change and got none: eGRID's own PLNGENAN implies a physically impossible 116.6 % capacity factor on 515 MW and a plausible 78.5 % on 765 MW, so the measured CHP rate was ALREADY a block rate charged to two thirds of the block. Against a same-HEAD zero-delta control the restored machine adds CC_CHP +1,013.7/+1,149.7/+1,073.3 GWh in 2023/2024/2025, displacing CT_PEAKER, CC_REGULAR, COAL_PRB, imports and ST_GAS, at max zonal |dLMP| 18.578/1.328/12.267 $/MWh and a one-sided system demand-weighted -0.0805/-0.0812/-0.1005 $/MWh. C1 CC_CHP error collapses -1.55 -> -0.53 and -1.61 -> -0.46 TWh (68 %/71 % of the class's whole error) because the EIA-923 benchmark target always counted this machine's output; summed C1 |error| improves 37.20 -> 35.46 TWh. Every criterion verdict, the determination and the ledgered caveats are IDENTICAL to the predecessor, with zero legitimacy-diagnostic changes. ZERO free parameters: the predicate is equalities on published EIA-860 categorical fields plus one physical vintage inequality (a heat-recovery steam generator is not older than the turbines that drive it), and the restored unit takes the block's existing rate. 50973 Motiva's 40.4 MW is deliberately NOT included -- a pre-registered falsifier and the vintage clause independently exclude it -- and 1004 Edwardsport, already represented as COAL 555.0 MW, is untouched. Promoted on structural fidelity under rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 14 [R-ACCURATE], never on a score.

THIS KEEPER'S OWN DELTA (miso-124): MISO's oil/gas switch-capable fleet is now priced the way the market prices it -- a unit flagged Multifuel on EIA-860 burns whichever fuel is cheaper, so its delivered price is min(gas, oil). The cap reaches 371 / 371 / 369 gas tranches (15,827 / 15,827 / 15,825 MW = 23.3 % of MISO gas) in 2023 / 2024 / 2025, with the parity price taken from 12/12 measured MISO F923 Petroleum months in every year (20.36 / 18.22 / 17.21 $/MMBtu -- the flat national fallback is never reached). ZERO free parameters: both legs are published measured registries and the mechanism is the arithmetic min() of them, with no coefficient between. It is INERT at every scored grain and that is the expected, measured result, not a failure: CAMPD's own meters put observed MISO dual-fuel oil generation at ~0.002 % of ISO energy, so the real phenomenon is too small to move an ISO-level annual criterion. Every criterion verdict, the determination and the ledgered caveats are IDENTICAL to the predecessor 2026-08-04-miso-122b-scope-gate; the whole price effect is 6 hours of mid-January 2024 (max zonal |dLMP| 1.383 $/MWh, system demand-weighted -0.000159), one-sided downward as a min() cap requires, and ~0.0003 TWh of class energy. Armed on rule 1 [R-STRUCT] structural fidelity under an explicit owner call, restoring an arming that miso-121 established and a merge race dropped.

THIS KEEPER'S OWN DELTA (miso-122): MISO's topping-cycle CHP plants are priced on a heat rate that no longer charges direct-fired host-process fuel to their power tranches. eGRID publishes ONE CHP heat-input split per PLANT, which cannot see a HYBRID cogen -- a topping CC/CT train plus a package boiler on the same ORIS code -- so plant 55088 Dearborn passed the derive's 0.50 unfired-topping ceiling on a plant-average thermal_share of 0.2396 while 16.6 % of its metered fuel burned in three 'Other boiler' units reporting ZERO gross load all year. CAMPD/CEMS resolves that at UNIT grain, and the derive now removes it: heat_rate = (PLHTIAN + CHPCHTI) * (1 - dark_fuel_share) / PLNGENAN. A SHARE, never an MMBtu subtraction, so it needs CEMS's fuel COMPOSITION to be representative and never CEMS's LEVEL to equal eGRID's; the denominator is unchanged, zero free parameters, no threshold, byte no-op wherever no dark fuel exists. Applied to 3 (plant, class) rows: 55088 CC_CHP (350 MW) and CT_CHP (165 MW) 8.3465 -> 6.9573 (-16.6 %), 10745 Midland Cogeneration Venture (1,479 MW) 8.8243 -> 8.8160 (-0.09 %). Against a byte-identical same-HEAD control: CC_CHP +0.3575/+0.2718/+0.5190 TWh and CT_CHP +0.2197/+0.2218/+0.2240 TWh, displacing CC_REGULAR, imports and COAL_PRB -- the correctly-priced cogen now runs where it should -- at max zonal |dLMP| 0.0491/0.0390/0.0752 $/MWh, under the 0.10 pre-registered bar in all three years. Every criterion verdict is UNCHANGED (12/12 free, 16/16 all, the same single C7 COAL_PRB shape FAIL). Promoted on structural fidelity under rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 14 [R-ACCURATE], never on a score, and it also closes a reproducibility seam: the predecessor keeper solved on the pre-gate artifact and stopped being reproducible from HEAD once the corrected input landed. Two dark-fuel plants outside MISO (NYISO 2493 East River, NEISO 1595 Kendall) are handed to their own lanes -- no parameter crosses an ISO boundary (rule 25).

INHERITED FROM THE PREDECESSOR KEEPER 2026-08-03-miso-117b-ct-heat, still carried and still true: MISO's CT_PEAKER fleet is priced on its OWN measured CAMPD loaded heat rates instead of eGRID's plant-average annual estimate -- 86 plants / 19,120.7 MW = 85.8 % of class capacity, zero rows excluded by the physical band, zero fitted parameters (rule 14 [R-ACCURATE]).
